settings.question: What blank sweatshirts are best for wholesale?
settings.answer: Midweight crewneck fleece sweatshirts are the standard for wholesale. The cotton/poly fleece is warm and structured, the flat crewneck front is an easy canvas for screen printing, embroidery, or DTF, and buying blanks by the pack keeps the per-unit cost low for full runs of spirit wear, staff shirts, or fundraisers.

settings.question: Crewneck or hoodie — which is better for printing?
settings.answer: Crewnecks are leaner and cheaper to decorate: there's no hood or drawstring to print around, and the flat front takes a logo or full-back design cleanly. Hoodies are warmer and read more casual. Both are midweight fleece and decorate the same way — Bayou stocks both, so pick the silhouette your design calls for.

settings.question: What is the best way to decorate a crewneck sweatshirt?
settings.answer: Match the method to your run and design. Screen printing is most cost-effective for bold logos in larger runs; embroidery gives a premium, textured left-chest logo or name; DTF and HTV transfers handle full-color art and short or one-off runs. All three hold up well on midweight fleece.

settings.question: Can you embroider a blank sweatshirt?
settings.answer: Yes — crewneck fleece is one of the best garments to embroider. Cotton-rich, denser fleece resists puckering and keeps stitches sharp; use a cut-away backing for stability. A left-chest logo (about 3–4 inches) is the standard placement on a crewneck.
